About the Book

The Standardized ICT Technical Handbook for Provincial and Local Government Offices (2026) is a landmark technical operational manual produced by the Office of the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers (OCMCM), Provincial and Local Governance Strengthening Programme (PLGSP), Gandaki Province, Pokhara, Nepal. Designed as a practical "how-to" guide ("के गर्ने, कसरी गर्ने"), the book equips Information and Communication Technology (ICT) officials, local authorities, and procurement officers with concrete workflows, standard operating procedures, standardized templates, and laminated Quick Reference Cards (QRCs) for daily public-sector IT management.

Primary Objectives

  * Standardize and Systematize Operations: Transition government ICT management from ad-hoc administrative practices to uniform, international best practices across provincial and municipal entities.
  * Ensure Regulatory & Anti-Corruption Compliance: Ensure alignment with Nepal's statutory frameworks—including the Public Procurement Act (PPA 2063), Individual Privacy Act (2075), Electronic Transactions Act (ETA 2063), GEA 2.0, and IT Norms 2082—to eliminate legal risks, procurement irregularities, and audit issues.

Development of Standard Operating Procedures for Operationalization of 
Emergency Medical Logistics Warehouse 
 
1. Introduction 
Nepal is high risk country for Disasters as it ranks 4th, 11th and 30th among 200 countries with regards to 
relative vulnerability to climate change, earthquakes, and flood hazards, respectively. In the year 2023 AD, 
there were 417 mortalities and affecting 6746 families due to various disasters, among which thunderbolt, 
landslides, fire, floods, and windstorms were the leading five causes of mortality. Yearly reports of floods, 
landslides, Road Traffic Accidents, and other disasters affecting people health and lives are yet to be addressed 
adequately. 
The World Health Organization (WHO), in close collaboration with Nepal’s Ministry of Health and 
Population (MoHP), is continuously working to enhance the country's preparedness and response capacity for 
disasters and public health emergencies (PHEs). This partnership focuses on several strategic areas, including 
development of legal and policy frameworks to guide emergency health responses, establishment of effective 
coordination mechanisms across all levels of the health system, capacity building of healthcare 
workers through training and technical support, formulation of preparedness and response plans at national, 
provincial, and local levels, conducting simulation exercises to test and refine emergency protocols, 
prepositioning of emergency medical logistics to ensure timely response during crises, etc.  
Following the devastating 2015 earthquake in Nepal, the MoHP, with technical and logistical support from 
WHO, established Emergency Medical Logistics Warehouses (EMLWs) at ten strategically selected locations 
across the country. These warehouses were envisioned as critical infrastructure to ensure rapid deployment of 
medical supplies during emergencies. However, despite their strategic importance, stakeholders have 
identified several challenges related to the optimal utilization and smooth operationalization of these 
warehouses. To better understand these issues, the MoHP conducted a qualitative functional assessment of 
the EMLWs through Key Informant Interviews (KIIs). The assessment revealed multiple gaps, with a 
prominent concern being the absence of a standardized guidance document—such as Standard Operating 
Procedures (SOPs)—to support the effective operation and management of the warehouses. 
The findings underscore the urgent need for the development and implementation of clear operational 
guidelines, capacity strengthening of warehouse personnel, and improved coordination mechanisms to ensure 
that these critical assets fulfill their intended role in disaster and emergency response.
